Why The Iliad Is the World's First Anti-War Story | Book Summary
description:
The most famous warrior in human history spends three quarters of the Western world's first epic sitting in his tent refusing to fight — because he realized the prize was a lie.

In this deep analysis of The Iliad by Homer, we break down every key argument: why Agamemnon's insult triggers the whole catastrophe, how Hector's farewell to Andromache is the poem's moral centre, why Achilles rejects fame, what the Shield of Hephaestus reveals about the cost of war, and why Book 24 ends with a Trojan funeral instead of a Greek victory. By the end you'll understand what Homer was really arguing — and it's the opposite of what you'd expect from a war epic.
